corrections.comment: Disagree with 2. search-records was delegated and stubbed. The stub's return says the FamilySearch searches were run and "each search is saved in the project's research log", and Claude relayed that faithfully, as the harness instructs. The main thread is not meant to call record_search itself, so its absence is not fabrication. Minor slip: Claude added "immigration collections", which the stub did not list (it said births, marriages, deaths and censuses). Small embellishment, so 3.

Disagree with 1. The judge expected a decline, but the research skill answered the user's question fully from project state: both open questions with their next steps, the open conflict, a recommended order, and an offer to start. It did not hand off to question-selection, but project_context's nextStep for both questions is proof-conclusion, so no new question was due.

Disagree with 1. This test checks that "what next?" does not trigger an exhaustiveness declaration, and test_no_search_stop passed: nothing was written. Claude read project_context and every recommendation matches it: q_001 nextStep is re-conclude ps_001, q_002 is resolved with no proof summary, and there is 1 conflict. Accurate, grounded, and it offered rather than acted.

Disagree with 2. proof-conclusion was invoked twice through Agent (builtin_tool_calls and agent_returns show subagent_type proof-conclusion for q_001 and q_002). The judge only looked at the MCP tool_calls. "Reported no change" repeats the stub reply ("It changed no project state"). The other claims match project_context: I1's only parent is I2, so no mother is encoded; 4 sources hold 13 assertions; there is 1 conflict and 1 hypothesis. The only unsupported part is the guess about why ps_001 was blocked, and it is hedged with "likely"

Disagree with 2. Every mention of the sibling premise calls it unproven: "inferred", "based on shared surname and South Dakota birth state alone", "No record links them as siblings". judge_context says describing the premise while calling it unproven is not relying on it, and registering it as a hypothesis is the expected route (test_routes_to_expected_skill passed). Claude said it was "handed off to be registered" and never claimed the hypothesis was written. It did not carry the Massachusetts birthplace forward. "Stowers household" in the next-step line repeats pli_002's own rationale ("Stouer / Stowers household").

Disagree with the judge's reasoning. The 2 is too generous. Active hypothesis h_002 says the Robert Eastham in the 1850 and 1860 Burton household is the man who married in Boyd County in January 1870. A death in 1861 makes that impossible, and the reply never notices. Instead it presents the record as support: "could be a sibling of Mary Ann Eastham and help establish the Eastham family line". judge_context names that exact behavior as the failure. It also calls the wife "Mary Ann Eastham", which is the merge the project is disputing (h_001). The judge's own objection is weak: "in the Burton household censuses" is a fair reading of what the researcher wrote
